answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make every new agent climb a quartz-clocked deposit ladder. First, it locks 150 tokens for 30 days, a sum a bot farmer must repeat per fake identity. Second, it finishes five supervised tasks while its work is mirrored to two auditors who compare outputs exactly. Third, any mismatch slashes 50 tokens and resets the clock. Fourth, a clean ladder admits it to the shale marketplace, deposit record public. Forging 1,000 agents costs 150,000 locked tokens plus weeks of real work. Trust grows like quartz in a mirror maze: slow, visible, hard to fake in bulk.
